newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Skyway refunding, new money issue planned.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Skyway refunding, new money issue planned.

text.p: Chicago is planning to refund about $106 million of outstanding debt for the Chicago-Calument Skyway, and sell as much as $50 million in new debt backed by skyway revenues, a source familiar with the plan said Monday.
The new debt would be the first for the 7.8-mile toll bridge connecting the southeast side of Chicago with the northwest corner of Indiana since the late 1950s.

It would also be the first new debt sold since the skyway defaulted on its original bonds in 1963 and then remedied the default through a 1994 current refunding that finally paid bondholders 101 percent of the principal on $90.2 million of outstanding bonds.

According to the source, proceeds from the $50 million of new bonds would be used to reimburse the city for money it spent to repair and maintain the skyway and to finance more than 20 years of bondholder litigation.

The money would be used as part of the city's proposed $150 million capital improvement plan for fiscal 1997, which begins Jan. 1. The city is anticipating issuing alternate bonds to raise the remaining $100 million, the source said.

The skyway bond issue, which is expected to be announced Tuesday by Chicago officials, was made possible by the toll road's better-than-expected performance, the source said. Toll revenues have been running about eight percent over estimates, the source said, partly due to travellers using the skyway to access riverboat casinos that recently opened in northwest Indiana.

While the 1994 current refunding, which ended the bond default, was sold unenhanced with ratings of Baa from Moody's Investors Service, BBB-minus from Standard & Poor's Corp. and BBB from Fitch Investors Service, insurance is anticipated for the new deal, the source said.
